divergences.description: Go returns HTTP 500 when MAC lookup fails (no NDS/ARP). Rust returns HTTP 200 with -1/-1.
divergences.fix_description: Rust usage_response now takes StatusCode param — returns 500 when no session (matching Go)

divergences.description: Go returns {status, quote, invoice, mint_url, amount, expiry, state, access_granted}. Rust returns {quote, request, pubkey} — completely different field names.
divergences.fix_description: Rust ln_invoice.rs response structs rewritten to match Go's lightningInvoiceResponse

divergences.description: Go returns {status, quote, mint_url, amount, state, access_granted, allotment, metric}. Rust returns {quote, state, checkState, expiry} — different fields.
divergences.fix_description: Same fix as D2 — GET response uses InvoiceStatusResponse matching Go

divergences.description: Go hardcodes socket path to /var/run/tollgate.sock (permission denied locally). Rust honors TOLLGATE_TEST_CONFIG_DIR for socket path.
divergences.fix_description: Go cli/server.go now honors TOLLGATE_TEST_CONFIG_DIR for socket path

divergences.description: Go CLI uses JSON wire format ({command, args}). Rust uses plain text (command args). Different protocols, not part of HTTP API contract.
divergences.fix_description: xfail in parity test — intentional protocol difference (JSON vs text)

divergences.description: Go resolves client IP to MAC via ARP/dhcp.leases, then looks up session by MAC. Rust uses IP directly as session key. Different client identification approach.
divergences.fix_description: Stub-level difference only — Rust uses IP as session key, Go uses MAC. Both return 500 locally.
